archetype.name: Rebuilding (offense ahead of defense)
archetype.definition: A young team coming off back-to-back 60-loss seasons whose offense now scores like a mid-pack unit while the defense remains among the league's worst, so wins come only when shots fall.

report.headline: Utah can score now; the defense is still the same bottom-tier problem.
report.take:
Three games in, the Jazz look a lot like the last two Jazz teams with a better offense attached. The 1-2 record is honest: W vs Pt Diff sits at 0, the one win was a 120-119 squeaker over New Orleans, and the losses to Memphis and the Lakers were by real margins. The site still puts them 16th of 30, a sign the roster rankings think more of this group than the result column does. That gap is the most interesting thing about them right now.

The offense is the real change. A 113.8 offensive rating ranks 11th, against a 22nd-ranked unit last season, and it is built on getting to the line (FT Rate 36.6, 5th) and crashing the glass (ORB % 29.3) more than on threes, where they take fewer than the league average and make 33.3%. Keyonte George has carried it: 65 points on a 69 TS % with the team's heaviest usage. Lauri Markkanen (62 points, +12.2 On-Off) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (59 points, 62.9 TS %) give them three real scorers, which is more than recent Utah teams could say.

The defense hasn't moved. A 123 defensive rating is 28th, after finishes of 30th, 30th and 29th the last three seasons, so this is not a small-sample scare. The shape of it tells the story. Utah keeps opponents away from the rim (Opp Rim Rate 26, 5th) and finishes possessions on the defensive glass (DRB % 76.2, 4th), but it forces almost nothing (Opp TOV % 11.7, 27th) and gets torched on the perimeter: shooting guards have taken 36.1% of the points against Utah, far above the league's 25%. The 38.3% opponents are hitting from three will cool. The lack of resistance at the point of attack, where the D+ backcourt lives, looks structural.

The lineup data hints at the trade-off the staff faces. With Jackson on the floor Utah has been 24.6 points per 100 worse, and Jaxson Hayes, more efficient at the five (77.7 TS %, +5.0 BPM), also carries a negative On-Off. Three games of On-Off is mostly noise, but if those numbers hold, the frontcourt mix will be where this season gets decided.

strengths.title: Free throws and offensive boards
strengths.body: Utah's offense lives on extra possessions and trips to the line rather than on outside shooting. FT Rate is 5th in the league and ORB % is above average, which is how a team shooting 33.3% from three still posts the 11th-best offensive rating. Rim pressure and size travel better than hot shooting, so this should hold up better than most three-game numbers.

strengths.title: George's efficient lead creation
strengths.body: George is taking the most possessions of anyone on the roster and scoring on a 69 TS % with 25 assists. That efficiency will come down as defenses adjust and his shooting normalizes. Even so, a backcourt creator this productive is new for a team whose offense ranked in the 20s the last two years.

strengths.title: Finishing defensive possessions
strengths.body: When opponents miss, Utah gets the ball: DRB % ranks 4th, well above the league average. The bigs also keep opponents out of the paint, and opposing centers have been held well under their norms. This is the sturdiest piece of a weak defense and matters a lot against Memphis this week.

concerns.title: A bottom-three defense, again
concerns.body: Utah is allowing 123 points per 100 possessions, 28th in the league, after finishing 29th last season and 30th the two before. Opponents are posting a 56.7 eFG % and almost never turning it over. With four straight years of this, three games of it is a confirmation, not a slump.

concerns.title: Shooting guards are feasting
concerns.body: Opposing shooting guards are scoring 45 points a game against Utah, 28th in the league, and account for 36.1% of the points it allows. That lines up with a D+ backcourt and with Darryn Peterson's rough start (-6.9 BPM, 46.2 TS %). Some of the 38.3% opponents are shooting from three is luck, but the point-of-attack leak is not.

concerns.title: Frontcourt minutes bleeding points
concerns.body: Jackson's -24.6 On-Off is the worst on the roster despite his efficient scoring, and his BPM is negative too. Hayes has been more productive per touch but also carries a negative On-Off. Three-game On-Off swings wildly, but if the two centers keep grading this way, the C+ frontcourt is propped up by Markkanen alone.

trend.note: Three games, no streak longer than one: a blowout loss, a one-point win, a nine-point loss. The margin and the record agree, and they look much like the last two seasons with a better offense attached.

weekAhead.headline: Memphis and Portland at home, Spurs twice: a winnable split
weekAhead.body:
Three of the four games are in Salt Lake, but two of the visitors are among the site's best teams. Memphis (3-0, 6th) already beat Utah by 20 to open the season and brings an A-graded backcourt straight at Utah's weakest spot. Portland (2-0, 2nd) leads the league in Net Rtg at 24.5 off two games and has smothered opposing wings and guards. Both are steep asks for a defense ranked 28th.

The Spurs home-and-away is where the week's wins live. San Antonio is 1-2, 19th on the site, with a 0.0 Net Rtg and an offense ranked 17th. Its defense has been giving up 41.7% from three and has let point guards score well above their norms. A realistic target is splitting the two Spurs games and stealing one of the other two; 1-3 is the likelier miss than 3-1.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis glass versus Utah's boards
keyMatchups.body: Memphis leads the league in ORB % at 37.8 and is 2nd in RPG, while Utah's DRB % ranks 4th. Second chances were a big part of the opening blowout loss; if Utah wins the defensive glass this time, the rematch is far closer. This is strength against strength, and the side that wins it likely wins the game.

keyMatchups.title: George and Collier against Spurs guards
keyMatchups.body: San Antonio has allowed point guards 11 points above their own averages, 28th in the league, with PRA allowed also 29th against norms. That sets up George, already scoring efficiently, and Isaiah Collier, who has 16 assists in limited minutes. Two games against this defense are the week's best chance to bank wins.

keyMatchups.title: Portland's three-point volume
keyMatchups.body: Portland takes half its shots from three (3PA Rate 50, 2nd) and has an A+ wing group, against a Utah defense allowing 38.3% from deep. Portland's 22.6% Opp 3P % over two games is unsustainably low, but its ability to bury a bad perimeter defense is not. Utah's path is the foul line, where Portland's FT Rate and opponents' trips have both been modest.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the shooting-guard leak closes: if Memphis's A backcourt and Portland's wings score at will again, the defense isn't fixable with this group.

restOfSeason.body:
The ingredients point to a better team than the last two Utah sides, but not a good one. The offense's foul-drawing and rebounding base is real enough to keep it around league average even when George's shooting cools, which alone should lift them past the 17- and 22-win seasons. The defense is the ceiling: four straight years near the bottom say it will stay there, and unless the team starts forcing turnovers and guarding the perimeter, a negative Net Rtg in the -4 to -9 range is the likely home.

The current 27-win pace already matches the margin, so there is no close-game luck to give back. I expect something in the 22-30 win range, with a defensive rating that drifts down toward the high teens as opponent three-point shooting normalizes but still sits in the bottom five. The 16th-place site rank flatters them on the strength of individual rankings; the results will lag it.
swingFactors: Whether the backcourt can contain opposing shooting guards
George's efficiency holding up at heavy usage
How the Jackson-Hayes center minutes shake out

confidence.note: Three games; On-Off and shooting numbers are noisy, though the defensive history is long.
